1. Validate the current bill: confirm meter reads imply 843 kWh (81,439 − 80,596), line items sum to $158.17 ($18.66 + $27.01 + $112.50), and the change vs last month is $7.99 ($158.17 − $150.18); flag any arithmetic mismatch as a potential billing error.

2. Map each billing period to its AEP Ohio tariff: last month (2026-02-28 to 2026-03-31) falls entirely under the pre-2026-04-10 tariff; the current period (2026-03-31 to 2026-05-01) straddles the 2026-04-10 tariff change, so prorate the fixed charge and blend per-kWh rates across the boundary.

3. Set days_usd = 0 because both periods are 31 days.

4. Estimate weather_usd from NOAA degree days: compare last month (CDD 3.5 / HDD 507.5) to current (CDD 56.5 / HDD 201.5), derive weather-driven kWh from the bill-history kWh vs. CDD/HDD relationship, and value that difference in dollars (or 0 if no defensible coefficient can be derived).

5. Compute price_usd from the tariff rate changes applied to baseline usage, then set usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly $7.99.

6. Check for a billing error by comparing the tariff-modeled current-period total to the actual $158.17; if the difference exceeds rounding, set billing_error_suspected = true and billing_error_usd to the discrepancy, otherwise false and null.

7. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
